commands.name: burn-scars
commands.help: refresh hazards.burn_scar from the fire perimeters in raw.record (the 'burn_scars' source does this hourly)

commands.name: wfigs-backfill
commands.help: load the approved Aug-Dec 2025 read of fire perimeters (made Oct 11, 2026; kept on the server) into raw.record (--load)

storage: Small, and only on change: under 1 MB a day typical, a few MB on a busy fire day (new perimeter versions at 10-100 KB each). The sources' records go to core's raw.record and evt.event (ch. 17 Q8). One table of its own, hazards.burn_scar (landscape sprint): the burn scars derived from the perimeters, a few dozen fires a year in the map box (under 5 MB), each refresh's tile version in core.layer_version. Transfer is about 60 MB a day before gzip (which we ask for), most of it the hourly FIRMS files (4 x 200 KB) and the USGS week feed (1.4 MB), cut to the ring before storing.
ethics: Road network and nature, not people: NWS alerts about people (Child Abduction, Blue Alert, Law Enforcement, Missing Person) are dropped before storing; FIRMS hotspots are pixel footprints, never pins on houses or structure-fire alerts; IDL's last_edited_user is dropped. api.weather.gov is robots-disallowed and never fetched (the WWA url field, api.weather.gov plus cap_id, is a link for display only). IDL states no license: internal, credited, until a courtesy note is answered (ch. 17 Q17).
